target_customer: Food creators and content companies who sell branded products, and partner brands who supply them
problem: Food influencers and content companies struggle to turn audiences into product revenue without handling tech, analytics and fulfillment.
business_model: marketplace with revenue share on creator branded shoppable products
product_category: social commerce and creator economy for food

founders.name: Ankita Sharma
education: Carnegie Mellon, Master's in Computer Science

founders.name: Madhuri Sharma
education: Boston University, BS in Film and Television
Institute of Culinary Education, Culinary Arts
founders.background_notes: YC page says the two are unrelated; her profile lists a later role at Publicis Groupe.

exit.reason: Cause not public; the YC directory marks the company Inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: A storefront and shoppable content layer on standard e-commerce tools; the harder part was operations and fulfillment of physical food kits.

defensibility.rationale: Creator relationships were the asset; creators could sell through Shopify or other marketplaces, and no exclusive supply is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Goldbelly later launched shoppable video in late 2021, per press; no source shows it affecting Global Belly.

market_need_then: Creator economy and social commerce were growing and the YC page reports 100+ food influencers launched and thousands of products shipped; no independent demand data was found.

identity.visual_style: Storefront for baking and dessert kits grouped by creator, per an older site snapshot.

branding.brand_signature: Creators called Tastemakers each get their own branded store.

rebrands.why: Per CB Insights only; the reason is not stated.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable food related name and a creator led store model, but no press about the brand, community or merch was found.

outcome_analysis: Global Belly built a marketplace where food creators sell branded products and grew to 100+ influencers per the YC page, then went inactive. Funding amounts are only in aggregators and conflict, and no shutdown reporting or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty. The site later showed a creator store marketplace for baking kits as of an older snapshot, which suggests the business ran for some time after the batch.
notes: Funding conflicts: Bouncewatch lists a $750K seed in April 2020 and about $1.05M over four rounds; CB Insights lists about $150K over four rounds with a June 24, 2020 convertible note, SOSV investor, and names YC and Food-X. Both rest on single aggregators; no press release or Form D found. The seed round entry uses Bouncewatch and may overlap with CB Insights entries. CB Insights also says the company was formerly Saffron Fix and founded 2014 in New York, which conflicts with YC (founded 2019, San Francisco); unverified. The website is live as an older snapshot with no shutdown notice and no founder names. Competitors left empty: Goldbelly shoppable coverage found is dated 2021 or later. Cause of inactivity not public.
